lesson.title: Scale Degrees
lesson.summary: Every note of a key has a number and a name that describe its place and its role in the key.

section.title: Degree numbers
section.p: The notes of a scale are its scale degrees, numbered upward from the tonic: the tonic is 1, the next note 2, and so on up to 7. The tonic an octave higher is 1 again. In textbooks the numbers are often written with a caret above them.
The numbers describe a note's place in the key, not its pitch. In D major, A is degree 5; in A major, A is degree 1.

section.title: Degree names
section.p: Each degree also has a name:

list.li: Tonic: the home note of the key.
Supertonic: the note just above the tonic.
Mediant: halfway from the tonic up to the dominant.
Subdominant: a fifth below the tonic, the dominant's mirror image.
Dominant: a fifth above the tonic; after the tonic, the most important degree.
Submediant: halfway from the tonic down to the subdominant.
Leading tone: a half step below the tonic, leading up to it. British English calls it the leading note.

section.p: The names are arranged around the tonic. The dominant lies a fifth above it and the subdominant a fifth below. The mediant lies a third above the tonic and the submediant a third below.

figure.caption: In G major: the subdominant C a fifth below the tonic, the submediant E a third below, the mediant B a third above and the dominant D a fifth above.

check.prompt: What is the fourth degree of a scale called?
check.explanation: The fourth degree is the subdominant, a fifth below the tonic. The dominant is the fifth degree and the submediant the sixth.

check.prompt: Which note is the dominant of G major?
check.explanation: The dominant is the fifth degree: G A B C D. C is the subdominant and F# the leading tone.

check.prompt: In Bb major, which degree is the highlighted note?

figure.description: A treble staff with a key signature of two flats. Four notes rise by step from the middle line; the last one is highlighted.

check.explanation: Counting from the tonic Bb: C is 2, D is 3 and Eb is 4, the subdominant.

section.title: Degrees in minor
section.p: Minor keys use the same names for degrees 1 to 6. The mediant is a half step lower than in the parallel major key, and so is the submediant, except where ascending melodic minor raises it.

The seventh degree has two forms. In natural minor it lies a whole step below the tonic and is called the subtonic. Raised by a half step, as in harmonic minor and ascending melodic minor, it is a leading tone, as in major.

figure.caption: In A minor: the subtonic G, a whole step below the tonic, and the leading tone G#, a half step below.

section.p: Usage varies between textbooks. Some keep the name leading tone for the seventh degree whatever its form, or simply speak of the lowered and raised seventh. This course follows the common North American usage: subtonic for the lowered seventh, leading tone only for the note a half step below the tonic.

check.prompt: In E minor, what is the note D called?
check.explanation: D is the seventh degree of E minor, a whole step below the tonic, so it is the subtonic. The leading tone would be D#, and the submediant is C.

section.title: Tendencies
section.p: Degrees 1, 3 and 5 are stable: a melody can rest on them, and the tonic is the most restful of all. The other degrees are unstable and tend to move to a stable neighbour.

list.li: The leading tone (7) rises a half step to the tonic. This is the strongest pull in the key.
The subdominant (4) tends to fall to the mediant: a half step in major, a whole step in minor.
The supertonic (2) tends to fall to the tonic, or rise to the mediant.
The submediant (6) tends to fall to the dominant. In minor this is a half step and the pull is strong.

figure.caption: In C major, four unstable degrees move to their stable neighbours.

section.p: These are tendencies, not rules: melodies often move otherwise. The pull is what gives a key its sense of direction.

worked.title: Find the leading tone of a key with flats

step.p: Take Ab major. The leading tone is degree 7, a half step below the tonic, on the letter below it: some kind of G.
The key signature of Ab major has four flats: Bb Eb Ab Db. G is not among them, so the seventh degree is G.
Check the distance: G up to Ab is a half step. The leading tone of Ab major is G.

check.prompt: What is the leading tone of B major?
check.explanation: The leading tone is a half step below the tonic on the letter below it. A is a whole step below B, so it must be raised to A#. Bb sounds the same but uses the tonic's own letter.

check.prompt: In a major key, which degree tends to fall a half step to the mediant?
check.explanation: In major the half steps lie between degrees 3 and 4 and between 7 and 1. The subdominant, 4, therefore lies a half step above the mediant and tends to fall to it.
